body.statement: The eigenvalues of \(\Sigma_4\) are \(121/100,99/100,99/100,81/100\), so it is positive definite and entrywise nonnegative. With \(N_{\exp}=1\), every connected balanced split minimizes Zhu et al.'s Section 3.2 two-cluster cut surrogate and \(H(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bal}};\Sigma_4)=29/50<59/100=H(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sing}};\Sigma_4)\), whereas \(V(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sing}};\Sigma_4)=826/25=33.04<968/25=38.72=V(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{bal}};\Sigma_4)\). Therefore exact minimization of \(V\) strictly improves on every surrogate-minimizing balanced split on this instance, even within the optional entrywise-nonnegative regime.
body.justification: The exact arithmetic proves that optimizing the published surrogate can select the worse full-risk connected design even on a four-cycle.
body.gap: Section 3.2 of Zhu et al. explains and justifies omitting the second-order residual-covariance term, but does not exhibit a connected design for which this omission reverses the full-criterion ordering.
body.consumer: The witness tells practitioners when candidate reranking cannot substitute for global exact optimization.
